lines: Three thousand years ago, this temple was carved into a cliff. In the sixties, engineers cut it up and moved it uphill.
The reason: the new Aswan High Dam was about to turn the Nile into a giant lake. The water would swallow the temple completely.
Step one: hold back the river. A temporary dam went up in front of the temple, so the crews could work in the dry.
Step two: take away the mountain. The rock above the temple was dug out from the top, until only the carved rooms were left.
Step three: cut it up. Workers sawed the temple into more than a thousand numbered blocks, some weighing up to thirty tonnes.
Step four: lift. Cranes carried every block up the cliff, to a new site sixty five meters higher and two hundred meters back from the water.
Then it was rebuilt, piece by piece, under a giant concrete dome, and covered with an artificial mountain, so it looks untouched.
Even the sunrise was saved. Twice a year, sunlight still reaches the statues at the very back, just one day later than before.
Four years and about forty million dollars later, the temple still sits high above the lake.
